name: chrome-devtools-mcp
one_liner: A tool that lets an AI coding assistant open a real Chrome browser, click around, read the page, and check performance and errors — so the AI can actually see and test the website it's building instead of guessing.
buyer: A frontend developer or agency using an AI coding assistant who's tired of the AI writing UI code blind and wants it to visually verify and debug what it builds.
business_use_cases: A dev agency wires this into their AI coding pipeline so the assistant tests and screenshots every UI change it makes before handing it to a human for review, cutting QA time.
A QA automation vendor builds AI-driven visual regression testing on top of it, using the AI to describe what changed between two versions of a page.
A performance-auditing consultancy lets an AI agent run and interpret Lighthouse-style checks across a client's site and write the report automatically.

money_ideas.idea: Build and sell a hosted 'AI QA agent' product that uses this under the hood to test client websites and send bug reports
Offer a one-off website performance and accessibility audit service where the AI does the testing legwork and a human polishes the report

steal_this: Build a simple service this weekend: point it at a URL, it uses an AI agent plus this MCP server to click through the site, take screenshots, and flag broken buttons or slow loads — sell it as a $20/month website health check.
